text:
sqlpipe moves data from Postgres to S3 in three stages: read, convert, and upload.

The reader connects to Postgres and streams rows in batches. It uses a server-side cursor to keep memory use constant. Each batch contains a fixed number of rows (default 10,000).

The converter receives each batch and builds a Parquet row group. It maps Postgres types to Parquet types and compresses the data. One batch becomes one row group.

The uploader writes the Parquet file to S3 as a multipart object. It starts the upload before the file is complete. If a part fails, the uploader retries it three times before it stops. When all parts succeed, the uploader completes the multipart upload.

The three stages run in parallel. The reader fills a buffer while the converter and uploader process earlier batches.
